description: Erection of canopy to rear amenity area.
decision_conditions: The proposed canopy, by reason of its width, height, depth, massing and proximity to the shared boundaries with Nos. 2, 3, 6 and 7 Cowley Mill Road, would result in an over dominant and visually obtrusive form of development in relation to these properties and would constitute an un-neighbourly form of development, by reason of overdominance, overshadowing, visual intrusion and loss of outlook. As such, the proposal would be contrary to Policies BE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One (2012), Policies DMHB 11 and DMHB 12 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020) and Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021).

The proposed canopy, by reason of its width, height, depth, massing, site coverage and design would appear as an unduly dominant, insubordinate and incongruous feature, detrimental to the visual amenities of the street scene and resulting in harm to the character and appearance of the area. As such, the proposal would be contrary to Policies BE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One (2012), Policies DMHB 11 and DMHB 12 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020) and Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021).

In the absence of a robust noise impact assessment that addresses the potential to increase users to the site, including any suitable mitigation measures regarding the control of noise nuisance from the site in relation to the nearby residential properties, the application has failed to demonstrate that the development will safeguard the amenities of those properties. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020) and Policies D3 and D13 of the London Plan (2021).

The proposed canopy is to accommodate overflow of visitors, and will provide for the potential to increase users to the site amounting to an intensification of use. The proposal fails to provide off-street car parking and, as such, is considered likely to result parking stress and congestion, thereby exacerbating existing parking problems, to the detriment of highway and pedestrian safety, contrary to Policies DMT 2 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020) and Policies T4 and T6 of the London Plan (2021).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

On this decision notice policies from the Councils Local Plan: Part 1 - Strategic Policies appear first, then relevant Local Plan Part 2 (2020), then London Plan Policies (2021). Hillingdon's Full Council adopted the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 1 - Strategic Policies on 8 November 2012 and the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 on 16 January 2020.
